title: EMA/EP for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
schedule_label: EMA on day 1, folinic acid on days 2 and 3, then EP with fluids on day 8.
schedule_summary: Dactinomycin and etoposide are followed by a 12-hour methotrexate infusion. Record its start time. There is no second day of IV EMA in this regimen. Start the first oral folinic acid tablet 24 hours after the methotrexate infusion STARTS. Take four doses 12 hours apart unless your team gives you a different written rescue plan. If a tablet is late, missed or vomited, phone the unit straight away. Etoposide is followed by cisplatin. Fluids are given before and after cisplatin to protect the kidneys. The complete cycle repeats every two weeks.
purpose: Treat the trophoblastic tumour with the aim of cure. Serial blood hCG measures how the disease responds.
indication_text: For high-risk GTN resistant to or recurring after EMA/CO, or GTN with liver metastases at presentation.
administration_text: Dactinomycin and etoposide are followed by a 12-hour methotrexate infusion. Record its start time. There is no second day of IV EMA in this regimen. Start the first oral folinic acid tablet 24 hours after the methotrexate infusion STARTS. Take four doses 12 hours apart unless your team gives you a different written rescue plan. If a tablet is late, missed or vomited, phone the unit straight away. Etoposide is followed by cisplatin. Fluids are given before and after cisplatin to protect the kidneys. The complete cycle repeats every two weeks.
monitoring_summary: Repeat blood count, kidney and liver tests. Check serum hCG on day 1, more often if indicated.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Dactinomycin
agents.explanation: Interferes with the way tumour cells use DNA to make RNA.
agents.mechanism: Interferes with the way tumour cells use DNA to make RNA.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately if the injection site burns or stings.
visual: Interferes with the way tumour cells use DNA to make RNA.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.
agents.mechanism: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse if you feel faint or breathless during the infusion.
visual: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.

agents.name: Methotrexate
agents.explanation: Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA.
agents.mechanism: Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA.
agents.watch: Check new medicines with oncology pharmacy and follow the timed rescue plan.
visual: Prevents rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells using folate to make new DNA.

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate.
agents.mechanism: Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate.
agents.watch: Ring the unit for any missed, late or vomited rescue dose.
visual: Supplies a usable form of folate to protect healthy cells after methotrexate.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Links strands of DNA together so tumour cells cannot divide normally.
agents.mechanism: Links strands of DNA together so tumour cells cannot divide normally.
agents.watch: Attend for fluids and blood tests. Report hearing changes or reduced urine.
visual: Links strands of DNA together so tumour cells cannot divide normally.

common_effects.title: How you feel between visits
common_effects.text: Tiredness, nausea or appetite changes can make everyday activities harder. Ask your team for help if symptoms interfere with eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: IV site injury · Dactinomycin
serious_effects.text: Report pain, swelling or blistering at the injection site immediately.

serious_effects.title: Sore mouth · Dactinomycin
serious_effects.text: Phone if mouth ulcers prevent you drinking.

serious_effects.title: Infection or bleeding · Dactinomycin
serious_effects.text: Contact the unit urgently for fever, chills or unusual bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Phone urgently for fever, chills or unexplained bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Infusion reaction · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, faintness or breathing problems.

serious_effects.title: Mouth ulcers · Methotrexate
serious_effects.text: Ask for advice if sores make eating or drinking difficult.

serious_effects.title: Slower clearance · Methotrexate
serious_effects.text: Attend kidney blood tests. Report vomiting or difficulty drinking.

serious_effects.title: Rescue tablets · Folinic acid
serious_effects.text: Check each time against your written schedule. Phone about a missed or vomited dose.

serious_effects.title: Hearing changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report ringing in the ears or trouble hearing conversation.

serious_effects.title: Kidney injury · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report reduced urine, vomiting or difficulty drinking.

serious_effects.title: Nerve changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report numb fingers, tingling or difficulty with buttons.

questions.q: What happens at my next visit?
questions.a: EMA on day 1, folinic acid on days 2 and 3, then EP with fluids on day 8.

questions.q: Which symptoms should I phone about?
questions.a: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness. Call promptly for reduced urine, ringing in the ears, new numbness, or missed rescue tablets.

questions.q: What should I plan before starting?
questions.a: Report hearing symptoms and medicines that may affect the kidneys.
After remission your specialist arranges hCG every two weeks for six months, then monthly for six months, then every two months for two years.

questions.q: Why does treatment continue after my hCG is normal?
questions.a: Three further cycles over six weeks help treat disease too small to detect. Your consultant may extend this to four cycles over eight weeks when adverse features such as liver metastases are present.

questions.q: What if I cannot keep fluids down after the day 8 infusion?
questions.a: Call your 24-hour oncology number promptly if vomiting prevents you from drinking or you are passing less urine. Cisplatin can strain the kidneys. Tell the team when you last drank and passed urine so they can assess whether you need fluids through a drip.

evidence.title: EP/EMA in resistant gestational trophoblastic tumours
evidence.interpretation: A specialist series supports platinum-containing salvage treatment after EMA/CO failure.
evidence.limitations: Non-randomised series with differing prior treatments. Follow the Irish sequence for administration.
